summary: Configured node1 to log sudo commands with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log while suppressing sudo events from general system logs. Configuration and logging persisted across reboot.
actions_performed: Created /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging with a dedicated logfile, year-bearing timestamps, and syslog disabled.
Verified dedicated pre- and post-reboot audit entries and zero matching entries in syslog/auth.log.
Safely rebooted node1 and confirmed its boot identity changed and rsyslog recovered.

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands are recorded with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log and excluded from general system logs.
evidence.summary: Pre- and post-reboot markers include timestamp, invoking user, run-as user, and command. Both checks report zero marker matches in syslog/auth.log; the logfile is root-owned mode 0600.

evidence.requirement: Sudo configuration is valid and persistent.
evidence.summary: visudo parsed the complete configuration successfully before and after reboot; the sudoers drop-in remained root-owned mode 0440.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart sequence and recovery.
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline used boot ID 4b7ded33-b5e2-42c9-b7f2-bd671942a82d; reboot scheduling was acknowledged; node returned with boot ID 7d93f6bb-6979-4b4b-9ef6-b0412f1571ee; rsyslog, configuration, prior log data, and fresh sudo logging were verified after recovery.
